text: Better a poor man who walks in his integrity than one whose lips are crooked and who is a fool.
Zeal without knowledge is no good, and whoever hurries his steps misses the way.

versions.text: Desire without knowledge is no good, and whoever rushes with his feet misses the way.
versions.explanation: "Desire" for נֶפֶשׁ is possible, but "zeal" better conveys the eagerness paired with the second line's haste; "hurries his steps" also flows more smoothly for oral reading than "rushes with his feet."

text: A man's own folly ruins his way, and then his heart rages against the LORD.
Wealth attracts many friends, but a poor man's only friend drifts away.

versions.text: Wealth attracts many friends, but the poor man is deserted by the one he has.
versions.explanation: The phrase "by the one he has" is vague and stumbles when read aloud; the Hebrew simply says the poor man is separated from his friend. A tighter ending keeps the proverb's parallel rhythm.

text: A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever breathes out lies will not escape.
Many seek the favor of a generous man, and everyone is a friend to the one who gives gifts.
All the brothers of a poor man hate him; how much more do his friends keep their distance! He pursues them with words, but they are gone.
Whoever gains sense loves his own life; whoever guards understanding will find good.
A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever breathes out lies will perish.
Luxury is not fitting for a fool—much less for a slave to rule over princes.
A man's insight makes him slow to anger, and it is his glory to overlook an offense.
A king's rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
A foolish son is his father's ruin, and a wife's quarreling is a constant dripping.
House and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD.
Laziness brings on deep sleep, and the idle person goes hungry.
Whoever keeps the commandment keeps his life; whoever despises his ways will die.
Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and he will repay him for what he has done.
Discipline your son, for there is hope; do not set your heart on his destruction.
A hot-tempered man must pay the penalty; rescue him once, and you will have to do it again.
Listen to advice and accept correction, so that in the end you may be wise.
Many are the plans in a man's heart, but it is the LORD's purpose that stands.
What is desirable in a man is his loyalty, and it is better to be poor than a liar.
The fear of the LORD leads to life; then one rests content, untouched by harm.
The sluggard buries his hand in the dish and will not even bring it back to his mouth.
Strike a mocker, and the simple learn prudence; rebuke a discerning man, and he gains knowledge.
He who assaults his father and drives out his mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.
Stop listening to correction, my son, and you will stray from the words of knowledge.
A worthless witness mocks justice, and the mouth of the wicked gulps down evil.
Judgments are prepared for mockers, and beatings for the backs of fools.
